'''Jon Nicholson Morris''' (born April 5, 1942) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for 15 seasons in the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Holy Cross Crusaders football|Holy Cross Crusaders]] before playing professionally for the [[History of the New England Patriots|Boston]] / [[New England Patriots]], the [[Detroit Lions]] and the [[Chicago Bears]].

Before entering politics, he played [[American football|football]] for 14 seasons as an [[tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was a participant in the [[2003 Pro Bowl]] following the [[2002 NFL season]]. He was selected by the [[Houston Oilers]] in the fourth round of the [[1996 NFL draft]] and later played for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and [[San Diego Chargers]]. '''Jon David Ritchie''' (born September 4, 1974) is an American sports radio host and former professional [[American football|football]] [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for seven seasons. He played [[college football]] at [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]] for two seasons before transferring to [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]], and was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the third round of the [[1998 NFL draft]]. He spent five seasons with the Raiders before signing with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in 2003, where he spent two seasons before retiring in 2006. Despite only 15 rushing attempts in his NFL career, Ritchie built a reputation with his [[Blue-collar worker|blue-collar]] work ethic and was considered one of the best blocking fullbacks in the league.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Battista |first=Judy |author-link=Judy Battista |date=January 24, 2003 |title=PRO FOOTBALL; Raiders' Ritchie Is a Studied Breath of Fresh Air |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/01/24/sports/pro-football-raiders-ritchie-is-a-studied-breath-of-fresh-air.html |access-date=September 19, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

After retiring from football, Ritchie entered a career in media. He has previously appeared as a contributor for [[ESPN]] and the [[NBCSN|NBC Sports Network]]. From 2013 to 2014, he co-hosted ''[[The Artie Lange Show]]'' alongside comedian [[Artie Lange]]. Since 2016, he has served as a co-host alongside [[Joe DeCamara]] on [[WIP-FM|94.1 WIP]] in [[Philadelphia]].

'''Jonathan Paul Dorenbos''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|ɔr|n|b|ə|s}} {{respell|DORN|boss}}; born July 21, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player and [[Magic (illusion)|magician]] who was a [[long snapper]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), earning two [[Pro Bowl]] selections.

Dorenbos played [[college football]] for the [[UTEP Miners football|UTEP Miners]] and was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2003. He also played for the [[Tennessee Titans]] and the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], with whom he played 11 seasons and played in 162 consecutive games. After getting traded to the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the 2017 preseason, it was discovered Dorenbos had an [[aortic aneurysm]] that required immediate surgery and ended his career. The Eagles went on to win [[Super Bowl LII]] that season, and it was announced Dorenbos would get an honorary [[Super Bowl ring]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theadvocate.com/new_orleans/sports/saints/article_c48b7058-0a2f-11e8-ac30-0bdf1f10b291.html|title= Jon Dorenbos, who had heart surgery after Saints trade, will get Super Bowl ring from Eagles |first=Joel A. |last=Erickson|work=[[The New Orleans Advocate]]|date=February 4, 2018|access-date=June 21, 2018}}</ref>

Dorenbos has a parallel career as a professional magician. He was a finalist on [[America's Got Talent (season 11)|season 11]] of the television program ''[[America's Got Talent]]'', performing his magic acts. He finished in third place for the season.
